card.name: Bidesia
card.tagline: Bhojpuri folk theatre of migration by Bhikhari Thakur
card.profile: Bidesia is a popular Bhojpuri folk-theatre form of Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh that fuses dance, drama, music and song, founded by playwright-performer Bhikhari Thakur (1887-1971), the 'Shakespeare of Bhojpuri' (Wikipedia; The Theatre Times). Named after his 1917 play 'Bidesia', it dramatizes colonial-era out-migration of labourers to Bengal and Assam and the suffering of the women left behind, addressing caste, dowry and gender injustice. Male actors play female roles using the launda naach style; instruments include dholak, harmonium, tabla, jhal and bansi, drawing on Bhojpuri song genres like biraha, purbi and kajari (Wikipedia; IJELTS).
card.insight: During 2009-2011 fieldwork in Patna, Vaishali and Nalanda districts, scholars estimated more than 200 active Bidesiya troupes still performing, showing the form's persistence as a vehicle of subaltern social commentary (Academia.edu).
